summary: A 1942 Army timber tower on Fort Lewis, replaced by steel in 1968, sold for scrap and rebuilt as IslandWood's Canopy Tower on Bainbridge Island by 2009.

facts.design: First tower (1942): 100 ft timber tower, L-6 cab with catwalk. Second tower: all-steel, 112 ft per the register and firelookout.com, built 1968 per those two (the IslandWood rebuilder instead dates it to 1966 and gives no original height; its page describes only the rebuilt tower, inconsistently, as either 125 ft or 118 ft).
facts.status_note: Site is gone; the second (steel) tower survives, relocated and rebuilt as Canopy Tower at IslandWood, Bainbridge Island.

access.note: Original site was on an active military reservation; no current access information found.

events.note: First tower: 100 ft timber tower with L-6 cab and catwalk, built by the U.S. Army on Fort Lewis Military Reservation
Replaced by an all-steel tower, 112 ft tall, per the register and firelookout.com
The firm that later rebuilt the tower at IslandWood instead dates the steel tower's construction to 1966, not 1968; it gives no height for the original tower
Rebuilder's account gives 1998 as when the steel tower was decommissioned and sold for scrap; the register and firelookout.com give 2000 for the sale
Register and firelookout.com: tower sold (and, per the register, moved to and sold again to IslandWood) around 2000

Reconstruction at IslandWood (Bainbridge Island) completed February 2009 by Sahale Snowkites & Climbing, reusing original Fort Lewis steel and adding a new ADA-compliant stairwell, stairs, catwalks and decks; dedicated under the name Canopy Tower in May 2009
Registered with the Former Fire Lookout Sites Register July 22, 2010, as US 559, WA 5, on a nomination by Irene Potter

notes_for_editor: Fact-check pass (2026-10-04) found the original story had miscited and conflated two of its numbers. (1) The 'five miles northwest of Yelm' location sentence was footnoted to the register (firetower.org), which actually says only 'Olympia, Thurston County' and never mentions Yelm; the Yelm distance comes from firelookout.com instead, so the footnote has been corrected to cite that source. (2) The steel tower's '118 ft' figure, footnoted as the IslandWood rebuilder's figure for the *same 1968 tower* the register puts at 112 ft, is actually that source's figure for the *rebuilt* Canopy Tower as it stands today at IslandWood -- and that source gives two different figures for that rebuilt height (125 ft and 118 ft) in two different places on its own page. The rebuilder's page gives no height at all for the original Fort Lewis tower, and separately dates its construction to 1966, not 1968 (a discrepancy the original story missed entirely). The story and this record have been corrected to state these distinctions rather than conflating them. Also fixed: the rebuilding firm was called 'Sahale Snowkites & Climbing' in the original story and source list -- that name does not appear anywhere on the cited page, which identifies the firm as 'Sahale LLC' (operating as Seattle Bridge Builders LLC); corrected throughout. The decommission-year disagreement (2000 vs 1998) and the general staffing/fire-history gap were both verified as accurately described in the original story and have been left as-is, with firelookout.com's agreement with the register's 2000 date now also cited. No staffing, named lookouts (other than 2010 FFLOS nominator Irene Potter), or fire-detection history for the Rainier site turned up in any cached or web source -- this appears to be a genuine gap in the record, not a search failure. The sibling record us-wa-rainier-lookout-site-at-islandwood gives height_m as 125.0, which is almost certainly a feet-to-meters unit mixup (125 ft, not 125 m, matching the 125 ft figure found on the rebuilder's own page) rather than meters; worth a human look at that record, though it is outside the scope of this task to edit it.
